record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Define C_∞(P) = ⋃_{k≥1} C(P^{∘k}), where C(P^{∘k}) is the semigroup of rational functions commuting with the k-th iterate of P. Is it true that there exist finitely many rational functions X_1, …, X_r such that a rational function X belongs to C_∞(P) if and only if X = X_j∘P^{∘k} for some j with 1 ≤ j ≤ r and some k ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Let us define the sets C∞(P) and Aut∞(P) by the formulas C∞(P) = ⋃∞_{i=1} C(P^{∘k}), Aut∞(P) = ⋃∞_{k=1} Aut(P^{∘k}).

Conjecture 3.1. Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Then there exist finitely many rational functions X1, X2, . . . , Xr such that a rational function X belongs to C∞(P) if and only if X = Xj ∘ P^{∘k} for some j, 1 ≤ j ≤ r, and k ≥ 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a rational function of degree at least two on the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$, and assume $P$ is non-special (i.e., $P$ is not conjugate to a power map $z^n$, a Chebyshev polynomial $\pm T_n$, or a Lattès map). For an integer $k\ge 1$, write $P^{\circ k}$ for the $k$-th iterate of $P$ under composition, and define
$$C(P^{\circ k}) = \{\, X : \widehat{\mathbb{C}} \to \widehat{\mathbb{C}} \text{ rational} : X \circ P^{\circ k} = P^{\circ k} \circ X \,\},$$
the semigroup of rational functions commuting with $P^{\circ k}$. Set
$$C_\infty(P) = \bigcup_{k\ge 1} C(P^{\circ k}).$$

Prove or disprove: there exist finitely many rational functions $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_r$ such that a rational function $X$ belongs to $C_\infty(P)$ if and only if there exist an index $j$ with $1 \le j \le r$ and an integer $k \ge 0$ for which
$$X = X_j \circ P^{\circ k}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is known to hold for tame rational functions: Pakovich proved that for a tame rational function P, the semigroup C_∞(P) coincides with C(P^{∘k}) for some k ≥ 1, which implies the finite-description statement in this case. For arbitrary non-special rational functions of degree ≥ 2, the conjecture appears to remain open in the general (non-tame) setting.

status_evidence.title: Tame rational functions: Decompositions of iterates and orbit intersections
status_evidence.snippet: For a tame rational function P the semigroup C∞(P) coincides with the semigroup C(P^{∘k}) for some k ≥ 1.
status_evidence.claim: For tame P, C_∞(P) stabilizes as C(P^{∘k}), implying the conjecture in the tame case.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions
status_evidence.snippet: For every non-special rational function P of degree at least two the semigroup C∞(P) coincides with the set of rational functions sharing an iterate.
status_evidence.claim: Structural results about C_∞(P) are known for non-special P, but a finite generating description as in the conjecture is not established in full generality.
